risks.title: Deterioration in macroeconomic conditions
risks.score_rationale: The risk is central in the 10-K, mentioned at the outset of the risk factors. The language is strong ("immediate and significant impact"). It is repeated as a primary driver of investment revenues. The Macro category is highly weighted for a financial player.

risks.title: Sector concentration in investment banking
risks.score_rationale: The text emphasizes that healthcare and financial services sectors weigh heavily on results. A downturn in either sector would have a disproportionate impact. The language conveys concern ("materially and disproportionately").

risks.title: Competition with larger players
risks.score_rationale: The risk is discussed at length, with mention of structural disadvantages. The language is explicit about the impact on revenues. The firm's smaller size is a recurring theme.

risks.title: Volatility of transaction-based revenues
risks.score_rationale: The transactional nature of advisory activities is presented as a major source of volatility. The text stresses the unpredictability of revenues. This risk is structural and repeatedly emphasized.

risks.title: Risks related to strategic acquisitions
risks.score_rationale: Acquisitions are key to growth, but the text warns of unforeseen costs, integration difficulties, and loss of key personnel. The risk is deemed significant for long-term strategy.

risks.title: Concentration in the municipal market
risks.score_rationale: The risk is specific to public finance operations. The text mentions dependence on municipal market conditions and tax policies. Less systemic than others, but significant for this division.

risks.title: Geopolitical shocks and armed conflicts
risks.score_rationale: Several geopolitical threats are listed (Middle East, Eastern Europe, Taiwan). The text explicitly links these risks to erosion in economic confidence. The tone is precautionary and repeated.

ai_positioning.summary: PIPR does not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F filing.
